title: Mark Twain: He Came In With Halley's Comet, and Left With It | Born 191 Years Ago Today

lines: He arrived with Halley's Comet, and left with it!
Who changed the world today? November 30.
Who changed the world today? November thirtieth.
On this day in 1835,
On this day in eighteen thirty-five,
in a tiny village in Missouri,
the writer Mark Twain was born.

data.hook:
He came with a comet,
and left with it
data.name: Twain

lines: His real name was Samuel Clemens.
He grew up in a small town on the Mississippi River.
When he was eleven, his father died,
and he went to work for a printer.
Whenever a steamboat docked, the whole town ran to see it.
His biggest dream was to pilot one of those boats.
In 1859, at twenty-three, he got his pilot's license.
In eighteen fifty-nine, at twenty-three, he got his pilot's license.
When crews measured the river's depth,
they called out: "Mark twain!"
It meant two fathoms, about twelve feet deep:
safe water for the boat.
In 1863, he took that call as his pen name.
In eighteen sixty-three, he took that call as his pen name.
And the world never forgot it.
In 1876, he published The Adventures of Tom Sawyer.
In eighteen seventy-six, he published The Adventures of Tom Sawyer.
Then came Adventures of Huckleberry Finn:
a boy and Jim, a man escaping slavery,
drift down the great river on a raft.
In the end, Huck decides: "All right, then, I'll go to hell,"
and he helps his friend reach freedom.
Hemingway said all modern American literature
Hemingway said all modern American literature
comes from that one book.
But bad investments left him bankrupt in 1894.
But bad investments left him bankrupt in eighteen ninety-four.
He was nearly sixty, but he didn't run from his debts.
Instead, he set off on a lecture tour around the world,
giving talk after talk, city after city.
A few years later, he had paid back every dollar.
He once said: I came in with Halley's Comet,
and I expect to go out with it.
In 1910, the comet returned, and he died the next day.
In nineteen ten, the comet returned, and he died the next day.
Today, his books are read in many languages,
and they still make readers laugh.
His question for you:
If you alone saw an injustice, would you stand up?
